topicTitle: Barriers to Integration and Measures for Cohesion
mdxBody:
## Social and Cultural Restraints

People might be marginalized and impeded from fully engaging in national integration initiatives by social barriers such as discrimination based on socioeconomic class, gender, race, or religion. Moreover, customs and traditions might also occasionally dissuade individuals from actively

Expand Your Horizon
From a linguistic point of view, Pakistan is a culturally rich country where around 70 languages are spoken. Through different sources, search the details of top 10 spoken languages of Pakistan.
participating, particularly women and minorities, which can limit their potential contributions. People from various linguistic origins may find it challenging to communicate and effectively connect with one another due to language disparities. Forming meaningful connections and relationships can be challenging for people with language problems.

## Institutional and Political Barriers

Lack of political representation is another barrier. People who think their opinions are not heard in the political process may feel disenfranchised. This may result in disinterest in and apathy towards initiatives to promote national unity. In addition, by refusing to back measures that foster unity and integration, ineffective or dishonest individuals and institutions can sabotage individual efforts.

Barriers Related to Geography and Infrastructure
It may be difficult for residents of undeveloped or remote places to obtain resources and take part in national activities. Communities might become isolated and find it difficult to integrate into the larger national framework due to inadequate infrastructure.

## Measures to Meet the Challenge

In order to get beyond these limitations and make the most of each person's contribution, steps must be taken. These actions can improve national integration and cohesiveness as well as socioeconomic advancement.

## Initiatives for Education

Providing everyone, regardless of socioeconomic status, with high-quality education equips them with the information and abilities necessary to make meaningful contributions to the growth of their country. There needs to be standards which are common for everyone so that everyone feels included. Moreover, encouraging civic education may help increase involvement in local and national events and increase understanding of the value of engaged citizenship.

## Expand Your Horizon

Article 25 (A) of the Constitution of Pakistan guarantees free and compulsory education to all children between 5 and 16 years of age. In the financial year 2024-25, the education budget of Pakistan has been increased from $1.5 \%$ of the GDP to around $1.9 \%$ of the GDP. Find more about the international commitments for education budget allocation.

## Economic Empowerment

Putting in place initiatives that generate employment opportunities and offer skill development can help reduce poverty and empower people to make more meaningful contributions to the advancement of society. Providing resources and capital to small enterprises and entrepreneurs can boost local development and spur economic progress.

## Appreciation of Diversity

Anti-Discrimination laws can help reduce disparity. By enforcing laws that oppose discrimination and advance inclusion, we can make sure that everyone has the chance to fully engage in national life. Moreover, various groups across the country might feel more united and a part of one another when cultural diversity is celebrated and supported.

## Developing Institutions

Good governance is the key to the success of the institutions. Increasing accountability, openness, and effectiveness in governmental institutions can boost public confidence and stimulate more civic participation. In addition, community-based organisations can also play a significant role. Individual efforts can be amplified and a more cohesive society can be created by supporting community organisations that promote integration and community development.

## Enhancing Infrastructure Facilities

Connectivity and access are also important to ensure inclusion of all communities in the national cause. Public infrastructure development, including public transport, communication networks, and roadways, can help to reduce distances between people and encourage involvement from
outlying populations. The more they keep in contact with different communities of the same nation, the more they understand each other.
By taking the above-mentioned measures, we can build an atmosphere where people may effectively contribute to the nation's socioeconomic progress and national unity by putting policies and programmes that support economic empowerment, inclusivity, strong institutions, and improved infrastructure into place.
title: Barriers to Integration and Measures for Cohesion

mdxBody:
## National Integration and Social Cohesion

In this unit the students will be able to:

- Explain the significance of individuals in shaping a meaningful society, community, and state.
- Enumerate the constraints of an individual's contribution in fostering national cohesion and integration while emphasizing the importance of supplementary measures in contributing to a country's socio-economic progress.
- Acknowledge the significance of the mutual respect and understanding exhibited among the diverse regional, cultural, religious, and ethnic identities in Pakistan, and the way it contributes to the creation of a peaceful society.
- Evaluate Quaid's vision for religious freedom and the role of minorities in the development of the state and culture of peace.
- Compare and distinguish the role of the state, society and government in establishing a welfare state that ensures equality, equity and justice on issues of gender, religion and social classes.
- Examine the elements that contribute to the unification and solidarity of a nation and their correlation with the challenges that impede these processes, specifically within the context of Pakistan.

## Role of Individuals in Shaping a Meaningful Society,

## Community, and State

Individuals play a crucial role in shaping a meaningful society, community, and state. Each person's actions, values, and contributions collectively weave the fabric of society, driving progress and fostering unity.

## Society

A society is characterised as a collection of individuals who interact with one another in a particular geographic or social setting and who share a shared culture, set of values, customs, and institutions. With numerous social, economic, and cultural facets, societies are intricate systems. They can be grouped according to mutual hobbies, language, race, or religion.

## Community

A community is a more intimate, smaller group within a society. Commonly used characteristics include a sense of belonging, a shared geographic location, and shared hobbies. Communities might be based on the same goals, shared living areas, or cultural or religious customs. Compared to the rest of society, members of a community frequently engage with one another more directly and frequently.

<CaptionedImage src="kg229eazfy8dazqs2vv8xryh0n8dhcm4" alt="" caption="" />
Pakistan Monument Islamabad

## State

A state is a geographically defined political entity with a steady population, a system of government, clearly defined borders, and the capacity to interact with other states. Typically, the government, judicial system, and security forces are the institutions through which the state exercises authority over its territory and citizens. States, which can be democratic or autocratic, are crucial for maintaining law and order, providing for the needs of the general public, and advancing the interests of the populace internationally.

## Role of Individuals in Society

Individuals who participate actively in civic duties, such as voting, volunteering, and engaging in community activities, help build a vibrant and democratic society. Their involvement ensures that diverse voices are heard and that societal decisions reflect the collective will. Moreover, by upholding and promoting values such as tolerance, respect, and empathy, individuals create a more inclusive and harmonious society. These values are essential for reducing conflicts and fostering a sense of belonging among all members of society.

Organs of the State of Pakistan are:
Executive: It includes the President, Prime Minister, Federal Cabinet, and Provincial Governors and Chief Ministers.
Legislature: Comprises the bicameral Parliament (Senate and National Assembly) and Provincial Assemblies.
Judiciary: Consists of the Supreme Court, High Courts, District and Session Courts, and special courts and tribunals.

Role of Individuals in Community
Engaging in community service and local initiatives allows individuals to address specific needs and challenges within their communities. This involvement not only improves local conditions but also strengthens community bonds. In addition, individuals who take on leadership roles or serve as positive role models inspire others to contribute positively. Community leaders can mobilize resources, advocate for change, and guide their communities towards common goals.

Role of Individuals in the State
Through entrepreneurship, innovation, and hard work, individuals contribute to the economic growth and stability of the state. A strong economy supports national development and enhances the quality of life for all citizens. Individuals who engage in political processes, whether by running for local, provincial, or national assembly elections, supporting candidates, or participating in policy discussions, help shape the governance of the state. Their involvement ensures that government actions align with the needs and aspirations of the people.
Individuals also have an important role in the cultural and social heritage of their nation. They help preserve and promote cultural heritage, traditions, and languages that contribute to the rich diversity of the state. Cultural contributions foster

<CaptionedImage src="kg2e26jxyk5sqyjb1ytkdsxn7h8dh48j" alt="" caption="" />
Abdul Sattar Edhithe Pride of Pakistan

Activity:
Think about a time when you, or someone you know, engaged in humanitarian activities. These could include volunteer work, helping those in need, community service, or acts of kindness. Write a brief paragraph describing your experience and share with the class.
After sharing, discuss the following questions:

- How do individual actions contribute to the overall welfare of the state?
- What motivates people to engage in humanitarian efforts?
- How can we encourage more individuals to participate in such activities?

national pride and a sense of identity. In addition, through artistic, scientific, and technological innovations, individuals drive progress and inspire societal advancements. Their creativity enriches the cultural and intellectual landscape of the state.
Constraints of an Individual's Contribution to Fostering National Cohesion
Although individuals are essential in promoting integration and national cohesion, there are a number of obstacles that may restrict their impact. In order to overcome these obstacles and improve the total effect of individual efforts, it is essential to comprehend these limitations.
Economic and Social Barriers
A person's capacity to advance society and the country may be limited by financial difficulties. People who have difficulty meeting their fundamental requirements might not have the time or finances to participate in civic duties or community activities.
A person's capacity to contribute meaningfully to both neighbourhood development and national debate may be hampered by limited access to education. Education gives people the information and abilities they need to contribute significantly.
title: Individuals, Society, Community and State

topicTitle: Pakistan's Diversity and the Role of Minorities
mdxBody:
## Diversity of Pakistan

<CaptionedImage src="kg218szwdtaj4x0q8fgd5tywfx8dgapc" alt="" caption="" />
Pakistan Motorways

Pakistan is a country abundant in cultural, religious, ethnic, and regional diversity. Embracing this difference with mutual respect and understanding can transform it into a powerful force that unifies us. It is imperative to acknowledge and appreciate the diverse identities present in Pakistan in order to establish a society that is characterised by harmony and peace.
Let's have a look at different kinds of diversity we have in Pakistan:

## Ethnic Diversity

Pakistan is home to a rich tapestry of ethnic groups, including Punjabis, Sindhis, Pashtuns, Baloch, Saraiki, Hindku, Kashmiri, Gilgiti, Balti, and other such ethnic groups. Each group brings its own unique traditions, customs, and social structures, contributing to the vibrant mosaic of Pakistani society. This ethnic diversity is a source of cultural richness and plays a vital role in the nation's identity and social fabric.

## Cultural Diversity

The cultural diversity of Pakistan is a reflection of its varied ethnic groups and historical influences. From the traditional dresses, music and dance forms like Bhangra and Khattak to the diverse culinary traditions found in different regions, Pakistan's cultural landscape is both dynamic and colorful. Festivals such as the Horse \& Cattle Show, Sibi Mela, Shindoor Festival and other such events are celebrated with enthusiasm, showcasing the country's deep-rooted cultural heritage.

## Religious Diversity

While Islam is the predominant religion in Pakistan, the country also has significant populations of Christians, Hindus, Sikhs, and other religious communities. This religious diversity is protected under the Constitution of Pakistan, which guarantees freedom of religion. The presence of various religious communities contributes to promoting a culture of coexistence and mutual respect.

<CaptionedImage src="kg2a1k5as7qppk0vqy349vk4f58dhf5w" alt="" caption="" />
Kalasha Community Pakistan

## Linguistic Diversity

Pakistan's linguistic diversity is extensive, with several major languages spoken across the country, including Urdu, Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashto, Balochi, Brahvi, Saraiki, Hindku, Kashmiri, Pahari, Shina, Broshiski, Persian and Khwar, among others. Urdu serves as the national language and a symbol of unity, while each region proudly uses its own language for everyday communication and cultural expression. This multilingualism enhances the cultural depth and connectivity of the Pakistani people.

## Geographical Diversity

Geographically, Pakistan boasts a diverse landscape that includes the towering peaks of the Himalayas and Karakoram ranges, the fertile plains of Punjab and Sindh, the arid deserts of Thar and Cholistan, and the scenic coastal areas along the Arabian Sea in Balochistan. This geographical diversity supports a wide range of ecosystems and climates, fostering a rich biodiversity and providing numerous opportunities for agriculture, tourism, and economic development.
This diversity must be welcomed and celebrated if Pakistan is to develop a strong and comprehensive national identity. A concerted effort to promote crosscultural dialogue, understanding, and respect for other identities contributes to social harmony and national unity.

## Mutual Respect for a Peaceful Society

Understanding and respect for one another are fundamental components of a strong and cohesive community. Respect for one another and an effort to understand one another among individuals and groups foster a positive atmosphere that increases collaboration, reduces conflict, and strengthens social cohesion.
Mutual respect is essential for promoting social harmony, building trust and cooperation among diverse groups, reducing conflicts, strengthening national unity, enhancing socio-economic development, fostering peaceful coexistence, and breaking stereotypes and prejudices. It is crucial to incorporate diversity in education, public awareness campaigns, community engagement, and supportive policies and leadership.
Education should teach students about the importance of diversity, respect, and understanding from a young age, promoting empathy and inclusivity. A rich curriculum should be developed that gives liberty to think and analyse. Public awareness campaigns can raise awareness about the benefits of mutual respect and understanding, while community engagement can be fostered
through interfaith and intercultural dialogues. Community events and celebrations can provide opportunities for people to learn about and appreciate each other's traditions.
Government policies should promote inclusion and protect the rights of all citizens, ensuring equal opportunities and fair treatment for everyone. Leaders at all levels should model mutual respect and understanding, inspiring their communities to adopt similar attitudes.
By fostering a culture of mutual respect and understanding, Pakistan can foster a more inclusive and peaceful society.

## Role of Minorities in Creation and Development of Pakistan

As mentioned earlier, Pakistan has a rich religious diversity and the Constitution of Pakistan gives rights to all its citizens irrespective of their religious background. The people belonging to religions other than Islam also played a significant role earlier in the creation and then in the development of Pakistan.
Let's have a look at their contributions to economy, education, healthcare, public service, governance, arts, culture and sports.

## Economic Contributions

Minorities in Pakistan have made significant contributions to the economy through various industries, including business, agriculture, and manufacturing. Notable minority communities, such as the Parsis, Christians, and Hindus, have been instrumental in establishing and growing businesses that provide employment and drive economic growth.

## Education and Healthcare

Minority communities have played a crucial role in the development of Pakistan's education and healthcare sectors. Many schools, colleges, and hospitals established by Christian missionaries and other minority groups have been at the forefront of providing quality education and healthcare services to people of all backgrounds.

## Public Service and Governance

Individuals from minority communities have held important positions in public service and governance, contributing to the administration and development of the state. Their participation in politics, civil service, and the judiciary has enriched the governance framework with diverse perspectives and expertise.

## Art and Culture

<CaptionedImage src="kg2dvthxk2r15sg71rs5cdgkd98dgq7k" alt="" caption="" />
Justice Rana Bhagwan Das

Minorities have significantly enriched Pakistan's cultural landscape through their contributions to arts, literature, music, and sports. Celebrated artists, writers, musicians, and athletes from minority backgrounds have brought national and international recognition to Pakistan.

## Quaid-e-Azam's Vision for Religious Freedom

Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah envisioned a state where religious freedom and equality were paramount.

Quaid e Azam believed that minorities played a crucial role in the development of Pakistan. He envisioned a nation where every citizen, irrespective of their religious or ethnic background, would have equal opportunities to contribute to the socio-economic and cultural growth of the country. Quaid's vision was for a pluralistic society where minorities could participate fully in public life, government, and the economy. He believed that by ensuring equal rights and protections for all, Pakistan could harness the talents and contributions of its diverse population, leading to a stronger, more cohesive nation.
<CaptionedImage src="kg2bm3pwn8qbpdgxtdxj8nbrhx8dg815" alt="" caption="" />

During a press conference in July 1947, Quaid-e-Azam said while replying to a question related to minority rights:
> "There will be no interference of any kind with their freedom of worship. They will have their protection with regard to their religion, faith, their life, their property and their culture. They will be in all respects treated as citizens of Pakistan without any distinction of caste, colour, religion or creed. They will have all their rights and privileges and also the obligations of citizenship. Therefore, the minorities have their responsibilities also and they will play their part in the affairs of the state. As long as the minorities are loyal to the state and owe true allegiance to it and as long as I have any power, they need have no apprehension of any kind."

In his historic speech on August 11, 1947, Jinnah articulated his vision for Pakistan, emphasizing that all citizens, regardless of their religious beliefs, would be free to practice their faith without fear or discrimination. He said:
> "You are free; you are free to go to your temples, you are free to go to your mosques or to any other place of worship in this State of Pakistan. You may belong to any religion or caste or creed-that has nothing to do with the business of the State."

This commitment to religious freedom was intended to foster an inclusive society where diversity was respected and all citizens could contribute to the nation's development.

Quaid-e-Azam's vision for Pakistan included the establishment of a culture of peace and harmony. He understood that respect for religious freedom and the inclusion of minorities were essential for social stability and national unity. By promoting tolerance and understanding among different religious and ethnic groups, Quaid e Azam aimed to create a peaceful society where conflicts were minimized, and cooperation was maximized. This vision of a peaceful and inclusive Pakistan was rooted in the principles of justice, equality, and human dignity, which Jinnah believed were essential for the nation's prosperity and cohesion.
title: Pakistan's Diversity and the Role of Minorities

topicTitle: Welfare State, Solidarity and National Unity
mdxBody:
## Welfare State

A welfare state is a governmental system that prioritizes the well-being and prosperity of its citizens by ensuring equal opportunities, equitable resource distribution, and social justice. In such a state, the government actively works to reduce inequalities and provide a safety net for all, particularly addressing issues related to gender, religion, and social classes.
In this state, equality means that all citizens have equal rights and opportunities regardless of their gender, religion, or social class. This includes equal access to education, healthcare, employment, and political participation. The state enacts laws and policies that prohibit discrimination and promote equal treatment for everyone.

Expand Your Horizon
Article 37 of the Constitutions of Pakistan outlines the state's responsibilities to promote educational and economic interests of backward classes, remove illiteracy, provide free and compulsory education, ensure just and humane conditions of work, and provide maternity benefits for women in employment. Can you find other Articles regarding a welfare state.

In a welfare state equity is also ensured that goes beyond equality by recognizing that different individuals and groups may have different needs and starting points. A welfare state ensures that resources are distributed in a way that addresses these disparities. This might involve targeted programs and support for marginalized or disadvantaged groups, such as women, religious minorities, and lower social classes, to level the playing field and provide everyone with fair opportunities to succeed.
Justice is another quality of a welfare state that involves creating a legal and social environment where everyone is treated fairly and with respect. This includes the protection of human rights, access to legal recourse, and the assurance that societal institutions are transparent and accountable. The state works to eliminate systemic biases and prejudices, ensuring that all citizens can live with dignity and security.

## Who Establishes a Welfare State?

Establishing a welfare state does not just rest on the shoulders of a government. This task is equally shared by both the state and society. Establishing and functioning a welfare state necessitates collaboration and interaction among the government, society, and state. Each person makes a distinct and valuable contribution to creating and maintaining a system that prioritizes the well-being of its residents.

The state formulates broad policies and constitutional provisions to ensure a framework of equality, equity, and justice. In contrast, the government is responsible for the day-to-day implementation of these policies through legislation and public services. Society plays a crucial role in advocating for these rights and holding the state and government accountable.
For instance, while the state ensures constitutional rights for all citizens, the government enacts specific laws like the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act to address gender equality practically. Civil society organizations advocate these rights and take necessary steps when these rights are violated.

## Role of the State

The state in Pakistan plays a crucial role in framing the overarching policies and constitutional framework necessary for establishing a welfare state that ensures equality, equity, and justice. The state sets the direction for social and economic development, enshrining fundamental rights in the Constitution of Pakistan.

Constitutional guarantees like Article 25 ensure equality of all citizens before the law and prohibit discrimination based on sex alone. Similarly, Articles 21 and 36 protect the rights of minorities, ensuring their inclusion and safeguarding their cultural, religious, and

<CaptionedImage src="kg29h42h8gsd0wgtvdkcnwner98dh022" alt="" caption="" />
Parliament of Pakistan

educational rights.
In addition to the constitutional framework, national policies also play an important role in a welfare state. National commissions on child rights and on status of women are to promote and safeguard child and women's rights.

## Role of Society

Society in Pakistan, through its various civil society organizations, community groups, and informal networks, plays a pivotal role in advocating for and implementing the principles of a welfare state at the grassroots level. Societal attitudes and collective actions can significantly influence the realization of equality, equity, and justice.
There are many nongovernment organizations (NGOs) and civil society platforms that work on gender equality and women's empowerment, advocating for women's rights and providing support services for victims of gender-based violence. Similarly, platforms like the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) focus on promoting human rights and addressing issues related to social justice, including the rights of marginalized communities.
In addition, there are many community initiatives such as Edhi Foundation that provide extensive welfare services, including healthcare, orphanages, and emergency relief, embodying the spirit of social justice and equity.

## Role of the Government

The government of Pakistan is responsible for implementing state policies, enacting laws, and providing public services that ensure equality, equity, and justice. Government actions directly affect the daily lives of citizens and their access to essential services.
Certain legislative measures have been taken by the government of Pakistan such as "the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010", which was enacted to provide a safe working environment for women and ensure their protection against harassment. To ensure minority rights, the Hindu Marriage Act 2017, Sikh marriage Act 2018, and Christian Marriage and Divorce Act, 2019 are important milestones that modernize and ensure fairness in the legal treatment of marriage and divorce for the communities belonging to different religions in Pakistan.
The Government of Pakistan also initiated important public services and social programs, such as the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP). This program aims to provide financial assistance to low-income families, particularly targeting women to enhance their economic stability and empowerment. Similarly Kisan Card, Hari Card, Sehet Sahulat, low cost housing scheme, youth entrepreneurship programs and other targeted programs are some other examples of steps taken by the Government of Pakistan.
<CaptionedImage src="kg27tnqwxfyyf2y8dvgp5c2hw18dgjxv" alt="" caption="" />

## Unification and Solidarity of a Nation

Protecting the country against internal and foreign threats to its security depends on the national identity being consolidated by national integration. There is a subtle difference between centripetal and centrifugal forces; the former creates an adverse environment with certain properties. This setting so affects several languages, cultures, races, and religions, all of which having the possibility to either contribute to national unity or fracture.

## Elements Contributing to Solidarity

There are several elements that contribute to national unity and cohesion. Understanding these elements is crucial for fostering a strong and united Pakistan.

## National Identity and Patriotism

Promoting a sense of shared identity and pride in being Pakistani helps unite diverse groups. Celebrating national symbols, history, and achievements fosters a collective national , consciousness. Incorporating patriotism into the education system through history lessons, national heroes, and the significance of independence can instill a sense of unity and pride.

## Inclusive Governance and Political Stability

Strong, transparent, and inclusive democratic institutions that represent all segments of society contribute to national unity by ensuring that everyone has a voice. Efficient and corruption-free governance that delivers public services equitably helps build trust in the state and promotes solidarity. In Pakistan, the upper house, the Senate is the symbol of equal representation of federating units.

## Cultural and Religious Harmony

Promoting dialogue and understanding among different religious communities helps build respect and reduce tensions. Encouraging the celebration of cultural diversity through festivals, arts, and cultural exchanges enhances mutual respect and understanding. Moreover, helping the youth to discover the diversity of the country by exposing them to different cultures may bring fruitful results.

## Social and Economic Equity

Ensuring that all regions and communities have access to economic opportunities and development projects reduces disparities and fosters a sense of belonging. Implementing social welfare programs that address the needs of the poor and marginalized groups helps create a more cohesive society. In this regard, it is crucial that more focus should be given to equity than equality.

## Awareness through Education

Educating citizens about their rights, responsibilities, and the importance of unity in diversity fosters informed and engaged citizenship. Responsible media and positive communication campaigns can promote unity by highlighting common goals and values.

## Challenges Impeding Unification and Solidarity

The processes related to the unification and solidarity of the nation are often challenged by various impediments. Some of these challenges are as under:

## Ethnic and Sectarian Divisions

Pakistan's diverse ethnic composition can sometimes lead to tensions and conflicts, particularly when certain groups feel marginalized or discriminated against. Religious and sectarian differences, if not managed carefully, can lead to violence and division, undermining national solidarity. The faith leaders from different sects and media must play a responsible role in meeting this challenge successfully.

## Political Instability and Corruption

Political instability, power struggles, and lack of consensus among political leaders can weaken national unity. This gets worse when the political leaders take extreme position that causes further polarization. Corruption erodes trust in government institutions and creates a sense of injustice, contributing to social fragmentation. Another adverse effect of the situation is when the government-allotted funds for marginalized communities do not reach them because of corruption.

## Economic Inequality

Unequal economic development across different regions can lead to feelings of neglect and resentment, undermining national cohesion. High levels of poverty and unemployment can lead to social unrest and hinder efforts to build a unified nation. It is important to offer special initiatives for such regions such as Aghaz e Haqooq e Balochistan and special initiatives for erstwhile FATA.

## External Threats

Extended external threats or disputes with neighbouring countries have the ability to divert attention and resources, therefore fostering an attitude of external adversary rather than internal cohesiveness. Pakistan borders India, hence previous conflicts and boundary disputes there, might sour diplomatic ties. With different regimes coming and going, strained relations with Afghanistan also pose threat to national security off and on. Periodic escalations or continuous confrontations can deflect national
<CaptionedImage src="kg2aammkj50eg750z82bmhjetd8dhsj0" alt="" caption="" />
focus and resources away from domestic problems, therefore, affecting attempts towards unity.

## Social Exclusion and Discrimination

Discrimination against women and gender-based violence impede social cohesion by marginalizing half of the population. Similarly, the exclusion of ethnic groups from mainstream results in feeling of being neglected. Failure to protect the rights of religious and ethnic minorities can also lead to social exclusion and tension, weakening national solidarity.

## Extremism and Terrorism
title: Welfare State, Solidarity and National Unity

## Challenges to the Tourism Industry in Pakistan

In recent years, due to change in different policies, Pakistan's tourism sector has demonstrated promising development. Nevertheless, its complete potential has not been realised in terms of economic and social progress. Despite its vast potential, the tourism industry in Pakistan faces several significant challenges that hinder its growth and development. These challenges include:

## Infrastructure Deficiencies

Many tourist destinations in Pakistan suffer from inadequate infrastructure. Poor road conditions, limited access to remote areas, lack of quality accommodations, and insufficient public amenities are common issues. These deficiencies make travel difficult and uncomfortable for tourists, reducing the attractiveness of these destinations.
In order to improve the situation of infrastructure in the tourist points of Pakistan, ample funds
need to be allocated so that better roads, transportation networks, and high-quality accommodations could be built or improved. In this regard, public-private partnerships can be encouraged to invest in tourism infrastructure, such as hotels, resorts, and recreational facilities.

## Security Concerns

Security has remained a major concern for tourists visiting Pakistan. The country has faced issues related to terrorism and bad governance, which have negatively impacted its image as a safe tourist destination. Although the security situation has improved in recent years, the perception of risk still deters many potential visitors.
These concerns may be tackled by improving the security situation through robust measures, ensuring that tourist areas are safe and well-protected. In order to guarantee the safety of foreign tourists and mountaineers in the Gilgit-Baltistan region, the Gilgit-Baltistan Police Department has implemented a high-altitude police unit. Similarly, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Murree Tourism Police have also been launched to facilitate and protect tourists in the resort station.
Another step could be launching international campaigns to highlight the improved security landscape and success stories of tourists who have visited Pakistan safely may also help improving the situation.

## Lack of Promotion and Marketing
summary: The economic, infrastructure, security, and promotional challenges facing tourism in Pakistan and sustainable measures for tourism development.

## Employment Opportunities

One major employment source in Pakistan is tourism. From hotels and travel to local artists and guides, the sector offers a broad spectrum of employment. The World Travel and Tourism Council(WTTC) estimates that around 3.8 million jobs in Pakistan in 2019 (about 6.3\% of all employment) were related to tourism.

## Infrastructure Development

As tourism grows, so does infrastructure including roads, airports, hotels, and leisure facilities. High tourist areas like Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Azad Kashmir have experienced improvements in infrastructure, which in turn helps local businesses and improves resident quality of life.

## Cultural Interaction and Maintenance

Travel helps to preserve cultural legacy and fosters cross-cultural communication. Attracting visitors to historical and cultural monuments allows Pakistan to support their upkeep and repair. Local businesses also gain boost because of cultural events, handcrafted goods, and local cuisine.

## Local Development

Through visitor spending and investment, tourism helps to boost local businesses. Tourism has brought economic uplifting to areas including Swat Valley, Hunza Valley, and the coastal areas of Sindh and Balochistan. This progress helps to lower regional inequalities and encourage national balanced economic development.
summary: The employment, infrastructure, cultural, and local-development benefits that tourism brings to Pakistan and its regions.

## Tourism

Tourism is the act of visiting a place outside of one's usual surroundings in order to pursue various goals, including leisure, business, religion or education. The economy, society, culture, and environment of the destination as well as the place of origin of the visitors can benefit or suffer from tourism.

Types of Tourism
Sightseeing, cultural exploration, adventure tourism, eco-tourism, and beach holidays are just a few of the several activities and experiences that make up tourism. Since it is so important for promoting economic deverapment, creating job possibilities, and enabling cultural connection, the worldwide business is of tremendous relevance. Travellers, sometimes referred to as tourists, engage in travel for a variety of reasons including relaxation, exploration of new locations, professional conference attendance, cultural exchange, and pursuit of fresh interactions.
Significance of Tourism
Tourism plays a vital role in recreation, offering individuals the opportunity to explore new cultures, relax, and break from their daily routines. It not only rejuvenates the mind and body but also fosters cultural exchange and understanding among different communities. In Pakistan, tourism is especially significant due to its rich cultural heritage, diverse landscapes, and historical landmarks that attract both domestic and international tourists.
Apart from improving human well-being, tourism is a significant leisure activity that significantly influences global understanding, economic development, and preservation of cultural legacy. Travel is interesting since it offers a broad spectrum of events fit for the goals and interests of people from many backgrounds.
Tourism contributes to the economy by generating revenue, creating jobs, and promoting local
businesses. It also plays a crucial role in preserving cultural heritage and natural beauty, as these assets become valued attractions that need to be maintained and protected.

France consistently ranks as the world's most visited country. According to the United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO), France attracts around 90 million international tourists annually.

## Famous Tourist Destinations of Pakistan

From historical civilizations and architectural marvels to spiritual sanctuaries and contemporary business hubs, tourism destinations of Pakistan highlight the numerous attractions. Apart from leisure enjoyment, visiting these locations enhances knowledge of Pakistan's cultural and historical inheritance.

Celebrated for their special beauty and relevance, Pakistan boasts a range of historical, religious, and commercial tourism destinations. Among the most well-known ones are these:
Historical Destinations of Pakistan
Pakistan features a great number of historical tourism destinations displaying the rich and varied cultural past of the country. Significant historical sites include:
Taxila
The archaeological site Taxila chronicles the evolution of ancient civilization from the Indus culture. It presents quite thorough proof of the several phases of development as shaped by Persia, Greece, and Central*Asia. Furthermore, it is thought that Alexander the Great visited this location at one time during his conquest of the area. It is a also UNESCO World Heritage Site. The site has stupas, monastic buildings, finely kept relics, Gandhara era sculptures.
Mohenjo-Daro
Located in Sindh, Mohenjo-Daro is one of the world's oldest planned cities, dating back to the Indus Valley Civilization around 2500 BCE. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its advanced urban planning, complex drainage system and architecture. Made of mud and baked bricks, MohenjoDaro is thought to have been one of the very first cities that spurred the Indus Valley Civilization and among the ancient major urban centres whose designs other civilizations, including Old Egypt, adopted.
Mehrgarh
Located in the Balochistan, Mehrgarh is one of the most important Neolithic (7000 BCE to 2500 BCE) sites

<CaptionedImage src="kg24m1a7gb0hh4bv6x8nz1jn1s8dh5bh" alt="" caption="" />
Mohenio-Daro

in South Asia, providing crucial insights into the early development of human civilization in the region. At Mehrgarh, archaeological discoveries include complex pottery, tools, and the first known evidence of dentistry. These finds point to sophisticated social, economic, and technological systems even before Indus Valley urban centres began to grow.

## Lahore Fort

Also known as Shahi Qila, the Lahore Fort is a perfect example of the rich architectural and cultural legacy of the Mughal Empire. It is also one of the UNESCO World Heritage sites. Originally constructed under Emperor Akbar's tenure in the 16th century, the fort was improved under later Mughal leaders, especially Emperor Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb, who erected elaborate palaces, pavilions, and gardens.

## Shalimar Gardens

Situated in Lahore, this UNESCO World Heritage site is a stunning example of Mughal garden design, reflecting the grandeur and sophistication of the Mughal Empire. Constructed in 1641 by Emperor Shah Jahan, the gardens are laid out in the traditional Persian style. The gardens feature 410 fountains, making it one of the most elaborate and beautiful Mughal gardens in the subcontinent. This UNESCO World Heritage site not only offers a glimpse into the opulence of the Mughal era but also serves as a serene retreat for visitors, showcasing the perfect blend of nature and architectural splendor.

## Takht-i-Bahi

Takht-i-Bahi, located near Mardan, is one of the most well-preserved Buddhist monastic complexes in the Gandhara region. Dating back to the 1st century CE, this UNESCO World Heritage site is perched atop a hill and offers a panoramic view of the surrounding area. The complex includes stupas, meditation cells,

A number of teeth found from Mehrgarh show drilling marks. It provides an evidence that during that time dentistry was common among people of Mehrgarh.

<CaptionedImage src="kg28phgtftkkzkzde3301fx3j98dhz9b" alt="" caption="" />
Nullmur Gitrikn

assembly halls, and living quarters, showcasing the architectural brilliance of ancient Buddhist monastic life.

The Rohtas Fort
Rohtas Fort, located near Jhelum, is a magnificent example of military architecture. Built under Afghan king Sher Shah Suri in the sixteenth century, this UNESCO World Heritage Site is known for its wonderful design. During the Mughal-Afghan wars the fort served as a fortified stronghold.

<CaptionedImage src="kg27cy4bcqftnb21p54x52g6858dhect" alt="" caption="" />
Rohtas Fort Jehlum

## Religious Tourism Destinations of Pakistan

Rich in both religious and cultural legacy, Pakistan hosts many sites of religious tourism drawing millions of people annually. Reflecting its diversified civilization, the nation's varied historical tapestry consists in important sites for Muslims, Hindus, Sikhs, and Buddhists.
Some of the famous religious tourism sites of Pakistan are as under:
The Badshahi Mosque
Located in Lahore, the Badshahi Mosque is a site with amazing construction. Built during the reign of Emperor Aurangzeb Alamgir, this massive mosque distinguishes itself among all the established mosques in Pakistan. The architecture of this mosque is its main draw; while it was built in 1671, the type of workmanship and skill used in its building is still a wonder.
Kartarpur Sahib

<CaptionedImage src="kg22s7ew5kz54fjmvywg7w5fmx8dgq1k" alt="" caption="" />
Badshahi Masjid Lahore

Located near Narowal, it is a significant pilgrimage site for Sikhs, especially with the development of the Kartarpur Corridor. It allows Sikh pilgrims from India and other parts of the world to visit the historic Gurdwara Darbar Sahib.
The Katas Raj Temples
The Katas Raj Temples, located in the Chakwal, are a complex of ancient Hindu temples that date back to the Mahabharata era. The temples are centered around a sacred pond. The site holds immense religious significance for Hindus and is a popular pilgrimage destination.
Gurdwara Panja Sahib
One of the holiest Sikh sanctuaries, Gurdwara Panja Sahib sits near Hasan Abdal, Punjab. It is linked to Sikhism's founder, Guru Nanak Jee, who is thought to have left his footprint on a boulder

Unit-08
near the spot. Particularly on the Baisakhi celebration, the gurdwara draws thousands of Sikh pilgrims from all around.
Jaulian
Jaulian, another important site in the Taxila valley, is known for its well-preserved monastery ruins. It features several stupas and numerous sculptures of Buddha, along with inscriptions and artifacts that offer a glimpse into the Buddhist culture and education system of the time.

Expand Your Horizon
Using different means find more about the religious tourism sites for Hinduism, Sikhism, and Buddhism in Pakistan.

## Commercial Tourism Destinations of Pakistan

Pakistan boasts several cities that serve as major commercial tourism destinations, attracting visitors with their bustling markets, modern shopping malls, and vibrant cultural scenes. These cities highlight the commercial vibrancy and economic potential of Pakistan, offering tourists a mix of traditional markets and modern shopping experiences. They are crucial for promoting tourism, supporting local businesses, ant showcasing the diverse urban culture of Pakistan.
Here are some of the key commercial tourist destination cities in Pakistan:
Karachi
Karachi, the largest city and economic hub of Pakistan, offers a diverse array of commercial attractions. Key destinations include Frere Hall, Zainab Market, Dolmen Mall, Sadar Bazar and Tariq Road.

Lahore
Lahore, the cultural capital of Pakistan, is renowned for its historical landmarks and lively markets. Major commercial spots include Anarkali Bazar, Liberty Market, Fortress Stadium, Emporium Mall etc.
Islamabad
The capital city of Islamabad is known for its modern infrastructure and upscale shopping destinations. Key spots include Aabpara Market, Centaurus Mall, Safa Gold Mall featuring numerous shops, restaurants, and recreational activities.
Rawalpindi
Adjacent to Islamabad, Rawalpindi is known for its bustling bazaars and commercial centers. Famous attractions include Saddar Bazaar, Giga Mall, Raja Bazar and other such shopping attractions.

Gujranwala
Gujranwala is well-known for both its strong sports culture and its industrial strength, particularly in the production of ceramics and pottery. The city has a mix of traditional bazaars and modern shopping centres, giving travellers a diversified shopping experience.

Sialkot is well-known for both its historical importance and active sports goods sector. Discover the old lqbal Manzil, the birthplace of poet Allama lqbal, and have a distinctive shopping experience for leather products and sporting equipment.
Gwadar
<CaptionedImage src="kg2cpgwyssqf0chx94gyk4m4d58dhre6" alt="" caption="" />

Driven by its deep-sea port, Gwadar is fast becoming into a vibrant commercial centre with modern amenities and great economic opportunities. Gwadar is an economically interesting area because of its strategic orientation and future development possibilities.
Faisalabad
Faisalabad, an industrial city, also has vibrant commercial areas. Clock Tower Market surrounding the iconic Clock Tower with eight bazaars, each specializing in different goods is the most famous commercial attraction of Faisalabad.
Importance of Tourism as an Industry in Pakistan
Tourism is a vital sector for Pakistan, that greatly boosts its regional development and national economy. Following are the areas related to promotion of tourism in Pakistan:
Revenue Generation
With more domestic and foreign visitors, Pakistan's tourism has exhibited notable rise throughout the years. The Pakistan Tourism Development Corporation (PTDC) estimates that the travel industry brought about almost \$1 billion in income in 2019. According to the World Travel and Tourism Council (WTTC), travel and tourism account for roughly 2.8\% of Pakistan's GDP overall, or roughly \$7.9 billion. This revenue is generated through a variety of channels, such as souvenir sales, food and beverage sales, accommodation, and travel and tourism services.

<CaptionedImage src="kg20zrz2qbz7w4s424akaex0918dh1zb" alt="" caption="" />
Pakistan Visitor Spending - World Travel \& Tourism Council 2024 Annual Research

By means of several projects, including the construction of tourism infrastructure, simplification of visa regulations, and promotion of Pakistan as a safe and appealing country, the government has been aggressively pushing tourism. These initiatives have resulted in higher tourism industry expenditure and more visitor visits, therefore augmenting income generation in the sector. According to the "World Tourism Barometer" published by the World Tourism Organisation (WTO) of the United Nations, Pakistan was the "best performing destination" in terms of tourism during the first nine months of 2023.

## Amendment procedure

A Constitutional Amendment Bill must be passed by both Houses of Parliament by a two-thirds majority.

## Major amendments

### The 8th and 13th Amendments

The 8th Amendment transferred important powers from the Prime Minister to the President. Article 58(2-B) gave the President power to dissolve the National Assembly, and decisions of the military government of General Ziaul Haq were exempted from judicial review. The 13th Amendment reversed these changes, limited the President's powers to dissolve the National Assembly and appoint armed-forces chiefs, and strengthened parliamentary democracy.

### The 14th and 18th Amendments

The 14th Amendment introduced Article 63-A to address political defections and breaches of party discipline. The 18th Amendment increased the authority of the Prime Minister and elected representatives, transferred seventeen federal ministries to the provinces, increased provincial autonomy, and introduced a new process for appointing judges of the superior courts.

### The 25th Amendment

The 25th Amendment merged the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It was implemented on 31 May 2018. The merger increased the membership of the provincial assembly from 124 to 145, including additional general, women, and non-Muslim reserved seats.
summary: Key amendments to Pakistan's 1973 Constitution and their effects on representation, parliamentary authority, provincial autonomy, and political stability.
title: Constitutional Amendments

topicTitle: Constitutional History and the Three Constitutions
mdxBody:
## Constitutional Development

In this unit the students will be able to:

- Discuss the salient features of 1973 Constitution particularly focusing on incomporating fundamental human rights, Islamic features and major amendments.
- Infer the responsibilities of good citizen, women rights, and rights of minorities in the light of 1973Constitution.
- Explain the federal structure of the government of Pakistan and its functioning in the light of 1973 Constitution.

## Historical View

The Constitution is the basic law of any state and is an expression of the thinking and aspiration of a nation. It contains the list of human rights and also explains the structure of a state and the form of government. The British Government entrusted the responsibility of drafting the constitution to the Constituent Assembly under the 3rd June 1947 Plan. On August 14, 1947, the Government of India Act of 1935 was adopted as an Interim Constitution. It remained functional with certain amendments until 1956.

## The Objective Resolution (1949)

The Prime Minister Liaqat Ali Khan presented the aims and objectives of the constitution before the Constituent Assembly. After the debate, a resolution was passed on 12th March 1949 and was known as the Objective Resolution. It was a significant and first step towards constitution-making in Pakistan. The salient features of the resolution are mentioned below.

1. Sovereignty: Sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to Allah, and the people of Pakistan will exercise governmental powers as a sacred trust within limits prescribed by Him.
2. The Constitution: The Constituent Assembly will frame the constitution for the sovereign independent State of Pakistan.
3. The Sate Authority: The State shall exercise its powers and authority through the elected representatives of the people of Pakistan.
4. The Islamic Principles: The Islamic principles of social justice, equality, democracy and freedom as articulated by Islam shall be fully observed in the country.
5. The Individual and Collective Lives of the Muslims: The Muslims shall be enabled to order their lives in the individual and collective spheres in accordance with the teachings of Islam.
6. Rights of Minorities and Marginalized Groups: The minorities will be given opportunities to freely profess and practice their religions and develop their cultures. Provisions shall be made to protect the lawful interests of minorities, backward and depressed classes.
7. The Federation: The areas currently part of Pakistan and any new areas that join will form a federation. The provinces will enjoy autonomy as prescribed in the constitution.
8. Fundamental Rights of the Citizens: The citizens of Pakistan will enjoy fundamental rights such as equality before the law, social, political and economic justice, freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith, worship, and association, subject to law and public morality.
9. The Judiciary: The independence of the judiciary shall be protected.
10. The Integrity of the Federation: The integrity of the territories of the federation, its independence and all its rights including its sovereign rights on land, sea and air shall be safeguarded.

## Importance:

The Objective Resolution has great importance in the political landscape of Pakistan. It laid the foundation for the future constitution of Pakistan. It was made part of the Constitutions of 1956 and 1962 as the 'Preamble'. It was declared as the 'Operative Clause' of 1973 Constitution during the rule of general Zia ul Haq.

## Delay in Constitution-Making

The 1935 Act was passed by the British Government to meet its colonial needs. There was an utmost need for a new constitution in Pakistan that could meet its political, social and ideological requirements. Soon after its creation, Pakistan faced gigantic problems, and the process of constitution-making was delayed. The following were the main reasons for the delay in constitution-making.

1. Initial Problems:

In the initial years, Pakistan has to face multidimensional problems. These issues delayed in the constitution-making.
2. Efforts for Constitution-Making: The following efforts were made to reach a consensus over the draft of the constitution. However, consensus could not be achieved, causing delay in the constitution-making process.
A. The Basic Principle Committee's First Report (September 1950): After the approval of the Objective Resolution in March 1949, the Basic Principle Committee was instituted under the headship of Liaqat Ali Khan. The important task of the committee was to determine principles for the future constitution. The committee instituted sub-committees to examine certain significant issues separately. The Basic Principle Committee presented the draft constitution in the Constituent Assembly in September 1950. The representatives of East Pakistan opposed the draft constitution. One of the important reasons for their opposition was the recommendation of Urdu as the national language. The draft of the new constitution was not passed by the Constituent Assembly. Liaqat Ali Khan was assassinated on October 16, 1951, and the process of constitutionmaking was delayed.
B. The Basic Principle Committee's Second Report (December 1952): Khawaja Nazimuddin became the Prime Minister after the assassination of Liaqat Ali Khan. He presented the second draft constitution in the Constituent Assembly on December 22, 1952. A Few recommendations are mentioned below.
I. The central legislature shall consist of two houses. Both houses shall enjoy equal powers.
II. The term of both houses will be five years.
III. The head of the state will be a Muslim.
IV. The head of the state will be elected by both houses of the central legislature.
V. The term of office of head of the state will be five years.

The leaders of the West Pakistan criticized the second draft. East-Pakistan's leadership also spoke against equal representation of both wings in the central legislature. Criticism continued on the second draft constitution and Prime Minister Khawaja Nazimuddin was removed from office on April 16, 1953.
C. Muhammad Ali Bogra Formula:After removal of Khawaja Nazimuddin, Muhammad Ali Bogra became the Prime Minister in 1953 and presented the third draft constitution in the Constituent Assembly on October 7, 1953. It was named as 'Muhammad Ali Bogra Formula'. Some of its features are given below.
I. There will be two houses of the central legislature.
ii. Both houses will enjoy equal powers.

iii. The seats of the upper house 'House of Units' will be divided among the five provinces on an equal basis. The total membership of upper house will be fifty members.
iv. The seats of the lower house 'House of the People' will be divided on the basis of population. The total membership of the house will be three hundred. One hundred and sixty five seats will be given to East Bengal (East Pakistan) and one hundred and one hundred and thirty five seats will be given to the province of West Pakistan, including the princely states and the federal capital.
v. Urdu and Bengali will be the official languages.

Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra Formula warmly announced that the new constitution will be promulgated in December 1954. However, Governor General Malik Ghulam Muhammad dissolved the Constituent Assembly on October 24, 1954 and the first constitution could not be promulgated.

## The Constitution of 1956

After a lengthy period of almost nine years, Pakistan was able to frame a constitution that was promulgated on March 23, 1956. The salient features of the constitution are mentioned below.

1. Written and Flexible: It was a written constitution and contained 234 Articles. It was flexible constitution that could be amended by $2 / 3$ majority of the National Assembly.
2. Federal Structure: Pakistan was a federal state and powers and functions were divided between the federal government and the provinces.
3. Parliamentary System: A Parliamentary System was introduced. The Prime Minister was the head of the executive and was to be elected by the National Assembly.
4. The Unicameral Legislature: There was unicameral legislature called the National Assembly. Its tenure was five years. There was equal representation of both Wings (East and West) in the National Assembly.
5. The President: The President was head of the state and enjoyed nominal powers. The candidate of the presidency had to be a Muslim.
6. The Governor: The Governor of a province was appointed by the president and was a representative of the federation. There was no fix tenure for the governor. He could serve at the pleasure of the president.
7. National Languages: Urdu and Bengali were declared as the national languages of Pakistan.
8. The Judiciary: The Supreme Court was the highest court of the country and the High Court was the highest court of the province.
9. Fundamental Rights: The 1956 Constitution contained a list of fundamental rights. A few are mentioned below.
A. All citizens were equal before the law.
B. There should not be discrimination on the basis of race, religion, caste and place of birth etc.
C. No person could be deprived of life and liberty.
D. No person could be deprived of legal property.
E. All citizens would enjoy freedom of expression and association.
10. Islamic Provisions
A. An Islamic Advisory Council was established.
B. The name of the country was 'Islamic Republic of Pakistan'.
C. The Objective Resolution of 1949 was declared as the 'Preamble' of the constitution.
D. The candidate for the presidency had to be a Muslim.
E. Laws had to be made according to the teachings of Islam.

## The 1962 Constitution

On October 7, 1958, President Iskandar Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution, imposed martial law and appointed Ayub Khan as Chief Martial Law Administrator (CMLA). Ayub Khan prepared a new Constitution and implemented it in 1962. The main features of the 1962 were as follows:

1. Written: The 1962 Constitution was in written form and contained 250 Articles.
2. Federal System: There was a federal system under the 1962 Constitution. Pakistan had two provinces: East and West Pakistan. There was only one list of powers and functions and the central government enjoyed extensive powers.
3. Unicameral Legislature: There was a single house of the legislature called the National Assembly. Its tenure was five years. There was equal representation of both the Wings (East and West) in the National Assembly.
4. Presidential System: In contrast to the 1956 Constitution, there was a presidential system under the 1962 Constitution. The president was head of the state and also head of the executive. He was elected by the members of Basic Democracies for a period of 5 years. He could be removed by the National Assembly through impeachment.
5. Indirect Elections: Under the constitution, the members of the National Assembly and the Provincial Assembly were elected by the members of Basic Democracies. Each province had its separate Provincial Assembly. There was also an indirect election for the president.
6. National Languages: Urdu and Bengali were declared as the national languages of Pakistan.
7. The Judiciary: The Supreme Court was the highest court of the country and the High Court was the highest court of the province.
8. Fundamental Rights: The 1962 Constitution contained a list of fundamental rights.
9. Rigid Constitution: The National Assembly had the power to amend the Constitution by 3/4 majority with concurrence of the President.
10. Islamic Provisions:
A. The official name of the country was 'Islamic Republic of Pakistan'.
B. The Objective Resolution of 1949 was declared as the 'Preamble' of the constitution.
C. The president was to be a Muslim.
D. The laws had to be made according to the teachings of Islam.
E. An Islamic Advisory Council was established. The president, the provincial governor, the National Assembly, and the Provincial Assembly could seek guidance from the council regarding the Islamic nature of any law. The council had advisory role and its opinion was not binding.

Analysis
The 1962 Constitution was framed by Ayub Khan and it was not prepared by any assembly. The President had extensive powers related to the executive and legislation. The process of removing the President was difficult, Ayub Khan introduced an indirect election method for the President, the National Assembly and the Provincial Assembly. Provincial autonomy was not ensured, and the federal government frequently intervened unnecessarily in provincial matters. Ayub Khan did not strengthen the system but rather strengthened the office of the President. On March 25, 1969, General Yahya Khan imposed martial Law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.

## The 1973 Constitution

The 1973 Constitution was a consensus-based Constitution and was prepared and passed by the National Assembly of Pakistan. It was promulgated on August 14, 1947. It is comprehensive and democratic compare to previous constitutions. The following are the salient features (Post-18th Amendment) of the 1973 Constitution.

1. Written: The constitutien is available in written form and contains 280 Articles, 12 Parts and 5 Schedules.
2. Federal System: Under Article 1, Pakistan is a federal state. There are four provinces: Balochistan, Khayber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Sindh. Islamabad is the federal capital.
3. High Treason: The Constitutions of 1956 and 1962 were abrogated by former military dictators. Under Article 6, if a person suspends, conspires or abrogates the 1973 Constitution, he will be guilty of high treason. The 18th Amendment 2010 strengthened democracy.
4. The Parliament: The Parliament consists of two Houses. The National Assembly is the Lower House and is elected for a period of 5 years. 336 seats are divided among the provinces and the federal area Islamabad based on population. The Senate is the Upper House and is a permanent institution. The total seats for the Senate are 96, out of which 92 are equally divided among four provinces whereas 4 seats are for the federal area Islamabad. Each senator is elected for a period of 6 years.
5. Parliamentary Form of Government: The Prime Minter is head of the executive and enjoys real powers. . The National Assembly elects leader of the house (the prime minister) and can also remove him from office.
6. The President: The President is head of the state and enjoys nominal powers. He is elected for a period of 5 years by the Parliament and the four provincial assemblies.
7. The Judiciary: The Supreme Court is the highest court, and there are five High Courts: one in each province and one in federal area Islamabad. The Supreme Court has the power to interpret the 1973 Constitution and to hear appeals against rulings of the High Courts. The Supreme Court's decisions are final.
8. The Provincial Government: Each province has its assembly elected for a period of 5 years. The chief minister is the head of the executive and is elected by the provincial assembly. The provincial governor is appointed by the President on advice of the Prime Minister.
9. Provincial Autonomy: Under the 18th Amendment, several federal ministries were devolved and transferred to the provinces. The Concurrent Legislative List was deleted from the

Constitution, and its subjects were transferred to the provinces. Now the provinces enjoy more powers.
10. Islamic Provisions
A. Islam is the official religion.
B. The Prime Minister and the President must be Practicing Muslims.
C. All laws shall be made according to the teachings of Quran and Sunah.
D. An Islamic Ideological Council has been instituted. It makes recommendations to the Parliament and the Provincial Assemblies for bringing existing laws into conformity with the injunctions of Islam.
E. A person who believes in oneness of Allah and Hazrat Muhammad as the last prophet of Allah is described as a Muslim.
F. Under Article 2-A, the Objective Resolution was made substantive part of the constitution.

Analysis
The 1973 Constitution was overhauled under the 18th Amendment. A genuine parliamentary system is evident in the country, with elected representatives enjoying real powers. The powers of the President have been reduced and democracy has been secured under amended Article 6. The Constitution contains more Islamic provisions compared to past two Constitutions. Now the provinces enjoy more powers than before. There must be supremacy of the 1973 Constitution, which will certainly strengthen the federation of Pakistan.
title: Constitutional History and the Three Constitutions

## Structure of Government under the 1973 Constitution

There are three organs of government: the legislature, the executive and the Judiciary. Following is the structure of the Federal Government under the 1973 Constitution.

1. The Executive: There is parliamentary system in the country and the Prime Minister is head of the executive. Under Article 90, the executive authority of the federation is exercised in the name of the President.

Cabinet: The Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly and nominates the cabinet. The cabinet members are taken from the Parliament. There are two types of ministers: federal ministers and ministers of state. One-fourth of the ministers are taken from the Senate. The President administers the oath of office to the Prime Minister and cabinet members. The Prime Minister can appoint five advisors. According to amended Article 92, the cabinet should not exceed eleven percent of the total membership of the Parliament. The Prime Minister is head of the cabinet and holds the authority to change the portfolio of any minister and can also take resignations.
The President: The President serves as the head of the state and is elected by the members of the four provincial assemblies and the Parliament for a period of five years. The President can be removed from office by a two-thirds majority vote in the Parliament. The President enjoys nominal powers and real powers are enjoyed by the Prime Minister and cabinet.
Accountability: Cabinet operates on the principle of collective responsibility and is answerable to the Parliament. Members of Parliament can raise questions, and the concerned ministers are required to provide answers. The Prime Minister and cabinet members are also Parliament members, and they participate in the sessions and can cast their votes. The National Assembly can remove the Prime Minister through a vote of no confidence. If the Prime Minister is removed from office then the entire cabinet is dissolved.
2. The Parliament: The Parliament comprises the National Assembly and the Senate.

The National Assembly: The National Assembly is the lower House of the Parliament and seats are allocated among provinces based on population. The National Assembly's term is five year. The Prime Minister can dissolve it under Article 58. It holds more powers compared to the Senate. It can reject money Bills but the Senate does not enjoy such power. The National Assembly elects its leader, the Prime Minister, and can remove him by a vote of no confidence. The minimum required strength for electing or removing the Prime Minister is fifty-one percent of the total National Assembly membership. Sessions are chaired by the speaker. Seats of the National Assembly have been divided under Article 51.

National Assembly have been divided under Article 51.

| Category | General Seats | Women | Total |

| Balochistan | 16 | 04 | 20 |
| Khyber Pakhtoonkhwa | 45 | 10 | 55 |
| Punjab | 141 | 32 | 173 |

| Federal Capital Islamabad | 03 | NIL | 03 |
| Non-Muslims | - | - | 10 |
| Total | 266 | 60 | 336 |

Note: Ten seats are reserved for Non-Muslims in the National Assembly
The Senate: The Senate is the Upper House, with seats equally divided among provinces. Each senator is elected for a six-year term, with half retiring after three years. Under Article 59, the Senate is a permanent institution and cannot be dissolved. The Chairman and Deputy Chairman Senate are elected for three-year term. Both, the Senate and the National Assembly equal powers for bringing the constitutional amendment. The total membership of the Senate is 96.

| Total | 58 | 17 | 17 | 04 |

The Judiciary: The Supreme Court is the highest court, comprising a Chief Justice and other Judges determined by the Parliament. The Judicial Commission of Pakistan nominates one person for each vacancy of a Judge in the Supreme Court to the Parliamentary Committee. The said committee consists of eight members, four from the Senate and four from the National Assembly. The committee sends the name of the nominee to the Prime Minister who forwards the same to the President for appointment. The retirement age of a Judge of the Supreme Court is sixty-five year. The Supreme Court resolves disputes between any two or more Governments, hears appeals, interprets the Constitution and also performs advisory jurisdiction.

## The Provincial Structure

Following is the structure of the Provincial Government under the 1973 Constitution.
The Executive: Under Article 129, the Chief Minister is the chief executive, with the Governor as the constitutional head of a province. The Provincial Assembly elects the Chief Minister by the votes of majority. The Chief Minister nominates the cabinet.
The Legislature: Under Article 106, each province has its own Provincial Assembly, elected for five years. The Speaker presides over sessions of the Assembly. The Chief Minister can dissolve the Assembly under Article 112. The Provincial Assembly passes the Bills and budget (money Bill). The cabinet members also attend sessions of the Assembly and answer the questions.
The Judiciary: Under Article 192, each province has a separate High Court. Judges are appointed
by the President under Article 175-A. The retiring age of a Judge of the High Court is sixty-two. The High Court exercises powers under Article 199.

## Process of Democracy

Process of democracy in Pakistan is mentioned below.
Elections: Elections are held at regular intervals for the National Assembly, Provincial Assemblies and local government. The Election Commission of Pakistan oversees the election process, ensuring free, fair and transparent elections.
Independent Judiciary: The Judiciary performs its functions in an independent atmosphere. The executive cannot remove the Judges from their offices. The Judiciary plays an important role in maintaining the rule of law in the country.
Political Parties: Pakistan has a multi-party system, with various political parties representing different ideologies and interests. These parties contest elections at different levels of government, advocating their manifestoes and agendas.
Voters: All citizens of eighteen year and above have the right to vote, regardless of gender, ethnicity, religion, or social status.
Parliamentary System: under the 1973 Constitution, Pakistan follows a parliamentary system of government. The Prime Minster is the executive head and is elected by the National Assembly.
Rule of Law: The principle of the rule of law is fundamental to democracy in Pakistan. It ensures that all individuals and institutions, including the government, are accountable under law.
Protection of Fundamental Rights: The 1973 Constitution guarantees fundamental rights to all citizens, including the right to equality, freedom of speech and expression, and the right to participate in the political process.
Media Freedom: A free and independent media works in Pakistan. It is a watchdog, holding the government accountable and providing citizens with information. Media freedom is necessary for democracy, ensuring accountability in governance.

## Important Constitutional Institutions

1. National Finance Commission: National Finance Commission (NFC) was established under Article 160. The NFC Award decides the distribution of money between the Federal and the Provincial Governments. The 7th NFC Award was signed on December 30, 2009 and was implemented on July 1, 2010. According to the 7th NFC, the allocation of share to the Provincial Governments is mentioned below.

The share of each Province under the 7th NFC Award is explained below.

|  | Total | 100 \% |

2. Economic Coordination Committee: The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) is a federal institution and the Prime Minister acts as Chairman. The Prime Minister nominates ECC's members and can also nominate any federal minister as its chairman. The ECC performs the following functions: It examines all urgent economic matters and coordinates the economic policies. It recommends the plans for the attainment of the status of a welfare state. It keeps an eye on the monetary situation of the country. It makes proposals to maximize production and export and to prevent inflation. It reviews from time to time country's import policy. It reviews social and economic surveys.
3. Council of Common Interest (CCI): The institution of the Council of Common Interest (CCI) was established under Article 153 of the 1973 Constitution. The CCI formulates and regulates policies in relation to the subjects enumerated in the Federal Legislative List (FLL)-II. The 18th Amendment deleted the Concurrent Legislative List (CLL) and also increased the subjects of the FLL-II. The 18th Amendment addressed the CCI and brought changes in its composition and functions. The CCI has to meet once in ninety days. The Prime Minister is the chairman of the CCI. Three federal ministers and four provincial chief ministers are also members of the council. The CCI submits annual report to both Houses of the Parliament. The true utilization of the forum of the CCI will certainly strengthen the federation of Pakistan and enhance the trust of the provinces upon the federal government.
4. The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP): The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) is a constitutional institution. The ECP consist of a Chief Election Commissioner and four members who are appointed for a period of five years. The ECP performs the following duties under Article 219.
- It prepares voter lists for election to the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies.
- It organizes and conducts election to the Senate.
- It appoints Election Tribunals.
- It holds general elections to the National Assembly, the Provincial Assemblies and the local governments.
